Host's Eagle The Host's Eagle was the largest eagle ever
known to exist.
It lived exclusively in New Zealand until around 1400 AD, which means while other
civilizations were building cathedrals and using gunpowder, the Maori were still actively
dealing with this thing.
Now, before you look at the size and relax, this bird weighed around 33 pounds
with a wingspan of 10 feet, which sounds manageable until you find out it regularly
hunted and killed the moa.
Assuming you are not built like a moa, a 440 pound flightless bird that was this
eagle's primary food source, you are already in better shape than most of its
typical victims.
It dove at up to 50 mph through dense forest, almost silently, with talons the
size of a tiger's claws, targeting the spine and pelvis simultaneously on impact.
